messages:
zoe: Proposal sketch: extract the "gatekeeper" responsibilities (authorization, tenant routing, plan selection) out of runtime into a tiny service. Goal: reduce runtime surface area and let platform teams iterate on policies without runtime deploys.

michael: Sounds reasonable. What exactly are we moving? Auth checks, tenant feature flags, routing table, and plan lookup?

zoe: Yes. Keep per-request hot-path as minimal as possible: runtime still validates tokens locally (fast path) but consults gatekeeper for policy decisions that change routing or billing plan. Gatekeeper publishes signed short-lived decisions.

anya: Concern: adding a network hop for policy decisions increases tail. Can we do cache-first with a signed decision to avoid sync on most requests?

zoe: Exactly 92 cache-first with TTL 200ms and signed decision tokens. Gatekeeper also streams invalidations for immediate updates.

sasha: KV locality again: if gatekeeper changes routing to a remote runtime pool we might blow cache locality. How do we prevent churn?

zoe: Gatekeeper will prefer sticky routing heuristics for recent prefixes; only reroute when capacity/policy forces it. We'll emit a "stickiness_score" in decisions.

ops-bot: CI: gatekeeper-proto branch build passed. Integration tests queued.

michael: Rollout plan? We need opt-in tenants, a passive observe mode, and a quick revert switch.

zoe: Phased roll: 1) Read-only observe (1 sprint) 2) Cache-first enforcement, opt-in tenants (2 sprints) 3) Global enforcement with regional gatekeepers (2 sprints). Revert = global toggle to ignore gatekeeper decisions.

anya: Metrics to watch: decision_miss_rate, routing_changes_per_minute, cache_invalidation_latency, tail_p99_latency. Set alerts: decision_miss_rate > 1% or routing_changes_per_minute spikes 5x baseline.

sasha: Ownership: I can do the streaming invalidation & regional agent, Michael takes telemetry + rollout, Zoe writes RFC and API.

zoe: I'll add example APIs and a tiny shim for runtime teams. Planning to draft RFC later today.
